title: Databases were revolutionised by one internal report
body: Edgar Codd's 1970 paper proposed storing data in relations and querying what you want rather than navigating pointers to find it. IBM, his employer, was slow; others built it, and SQL databases followed. Codd had to argue that a mathematical model beat hand-tuned access paths, and he was right.
source_hint: Codd, 'A Relational Model of Data for Large Shared Data Banks' (1970)
